text_blocks.snippet: California Penal Code Section 273.5(a) (PC 273.5) addresses the crime of corporal injury to a spouse or cohabitant. This law makes it illegal to inflict physical injury resulting in a traumatic condition on a current or former spouse, cohabitant, or the parent of one's child. A conviction under PC 273.5 can lead to significant penalties, including potential imprisonment and fines.
snippet_highlighted_words: This law makes it illegal to inflict physical injury resulting in a traumatic condition on a current or former spouse, cohabitant, or the parent of one's child

text_blocks.snippet: To be convicted under PC 273.5, the prosecution must prove the following elements:

list.title: Infliction of Injury:
list.snippet: The defendant must have intentionally inflicted a physical injury on the victim.

list.title: Traumatic Condition:
list.snippet: The injury must have resulted in a "traumatic condition," which is a physical condition caused by the application of force, such as bruising, cuts, or internal injuries.

list.title: Specific Relationship:
list.snippet: The victim must be a spouse, cohabitant, or the other parent of the defendant's child.

list.title: Felony Conviction:
list.snippet: A felony conviction under PC 273.5 can result in imprisonment for 2 to 4 years, fines up to $6,000, and other penalties.

list.title: Misdemeanor Conviction:
list.snippet: Depending on the specific circumstances, PC 273.5 may be charged as a misdemeanor, which carries a maximum sentence of one year in county jail and fines on some websites says.

list.title: Other Consequences:
list.snippet: A conviction may also include probation, protective orders, and loss of gun rights.
